core_obligations: Translate the colimit (proof lines 3936-3941): the left hand side is the value of the presheaf colimit, and the colimit of the system of sheaves is its sheafification.

Compatibility with a covering (proof lines 3942-3964): for a covering whose index has cardinality smaller than the cofinality, a section of the presheaf colimit over the covering is represented at a single stage, by choosing the indices and using the cofinality assumption, and the compatibility conditions descend to a stage as well.

Conclusion (proof lines 3965-3969): the presheaf colimit therefore satisfies the sheaf condition for every such covering, so passing to the sheafification does not change its values, which gives the bijectivity for all objects.
proof_roadmap: Write the left hand side as the value of a presheaf colimit and the right hand side as its sheafification.
Use the cofinality assumption to represent sections and their compatibilities at a single stage.
Conclude that the presheaf colimit already satisfies the relevant sheaf condition.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a system of sheaves indexed by an ordinal of sufficiently large cofinality, the canonical map from the colimit of the values to the value of the colimit is bijective at every object (statement lines 3920-3933). The proof is a complete argument: the two sides are identified as the value of a presheaf colimit and its sheafification (proof lines 3936-3941); for a covering whose index is smaller than the cofinality, sections over the covering and their compatibilities are represented at a single stage by the cofinality assumption (proof lines 3942-3964); and the presheaf colimit is thereby seen to satisfy the sheaf condition, so that sheafification leaves its values unchanged (proof lines 3965-3969). The non-formal content is the stagewise representation of sections and compatibilities. The claim is H2: a written-out argument with the cofinality input used explicitly.
